scores.criterion: Introduction and background (assembly language, architecture, system calls, project overview, assumptions)
scores.justification: The explanation of architecture and flag mechanics is somewhat brief and contains minor typographical errors ('N Navigation applications'). However, Section 1.2 provides excellent project-specific tables mapping the IA-32 registers (Table 1) and Linux int 0x80 system calls (Table 2) alongside 8 realistic domain assumptions.

scores.criterion: Research and critical analysis (relevance of assembly, areas of use, cyber security / forensics / malware analysis, case studies, practical demonstration)
scores.justification: Section 2.2.1 ('Embedded and Real-Time Systems') is an accidental verbatim copy-paste of Section 2.1, meaning embedded systems are not actually analysed. This gap is offset by an outstanding 5-step practical reverse engineering demonstration (Section 2.4) that strips, disassembles, profiles syscalls, and patches the student's own ELF binary.

The prose description of the signal phase model in Section 3.2 contains minor inaccuracies regarding when the walk and emergency durations are added compared to Table 6. Overall, the design is thorough and well-structured, featuring a six-phase state table, clear modular descriptions, and detailed data design in Table 7 ('prof_tab 4 entries x 24 bytes', 'cfg_tab 7 entries x 24 bytes').

scores.criterion: Implementation of the required constructs (ADD/SUB, loops, conditional and unconditional jumps, input validation) with explanation
scores.justification: Only code excerpts are embedded in the report rather than the full 1,700-line assembly listing, and error recovery paths in some snippets (such as '.bad' in 'read_int_range') are truncated. Nevertheless, the code demonstrates strong low-level mastery across all required constructs, including 'sub eax, [ns_green]', nested 'loop' and 'dec ecx / jnz .subtick' timing loops, conditional branching, and raw terminal polling via 'sys_ioctl' and 'sys_poll'.

Test cases in Table 9 summarize expected and actual results briefly without showing raw input/output logs for every boundary condition in the table itself. However, the 18 test cases cover critical edge cases (invalid input, duplicate requests, '/dev/null' EOF, 'Ctrl+C' signal handling), and the user manual includes comprehensive cross-platform build instructions (x86 and ARM QEMU) and troubleshooting.

Section 7.0 (Conclusion) ends abruptly mid-sentence ('adjusting green time depending on'), four entries in the reference list (Barr & Massa, VirusTotal, Yiu) are not cited in the text, and Appendix B.2 Prompt 1 contradicts the summary table by showing a prompt about the 'cat' command. Otherwise, APA referencing is properly formatted and well-integrated throughout the report.
